title: Future Forms: Will vs. Going To
subtitle: Choose between a spontaneous decision and a plan already made.
objectives: Use "will" for spontaneous decisions, predictions, offers and promises
Use "going to" for plans and intentions decided before now
Use "going to" for predictions based on present evidence

content.intro: Both describe the future, but they answer a different question: was this decided just now, or before now?

rules.heading: a) Will
rules.body:
• Spontaneous decision (decided at the moment of speaking): The phone's ringing — I'll get it.
  • Prediction/opinion (no evidence, just belief): I think it will rain tomorrow.
  • Offers and promises: I'll help you with that. / I promise I'll call you.

rules.heading: b) Going to
rules.body:
• Plan/intention (decided before now): I'm going to visit my parents this weekend. (already decided)
  • Prediction based on present evidence: Look at those clouds — it's going to rain.

examples: The phone's ringing — I'll get it.
I'm going to visit my parents this weekend.
I think it will rain tomorrow.
Look at those clouds — it's going to rain.
We're going to buy a new car next month.

commonMistakes.wrong: I'm going to visit my parents. (decided right now, spontaneously)
commonMistakes.right: I'll visit my parents. / I'm going to visit my parents.
commonMistakes.why: A decision made at the moment of speaking uses "will"; a plan decided earlier uses "going to" — check which situation applies before choosing.

commonMistakes.wrong: Look at those clouds — it will rain.
commonMistakes.right: Look at those clouds — it's going to rain.
commonMistakes.why: A prediction based on visible present evidence needs "going to," not "will."

commonMistakes.wrong: I go to visit my parents this weekend.
commonMistakes.right: I'm going to visit my parents this weekend.
commonMistakes.why: "Going to" needs the full form "am/is/are going to," not just "go to."

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with will or the correct form of going to.

items.explanation: A spontaneous decision at the moment of speaking — "will."

items.prompt: I ___ (visit) my parents this weekend. (already planned)
items.explanation: A plan decided before now — "going to."

items.prompt: Look at those clouds — it ___ (rain). (visible evidence)
items.explanation: A prediction based on present evidence — "going to."

items.prompt: I think it ___ (be) sunny tomorrow. (opinion, no evidence)
items.explanation: A prediction based on opinion, not evidence — "will."

items.prompt: I promise I ___ call you tomorrow.
We ___ buy a new car next month. (decided last week)
items.explanation: A plan decided before now — "going to."

items.incorrect: Look at the sky — it will rain.
answer: Look at the sky — it's going to rain.

items.incorrect: I go to visit my parents this weekend.
answer: I'm going to visit my parents this weekend.

summary: Will = spontaneous decisions, opinions/predictions without evidence, offers, promises.
Going to = plans decided before now, and predictions based on visible present evidence.
Ask: was this decided right now, or before? And is there evidence I can see?
